title: Parsimony block: a compact harmonic fit
summary: This implementation first smooths the observed series, then projects the remaining signal onto cosine and sine columns at a supplied period. It is a fixed-basis least-squares operator. The trace makes the design matrix, fitted coefficients and additive contributions visible; it does not reproduce a complete forecasting architecture from the cited paper.

steps.title: Remove a smoothed trend
steps.text: Estimate the trend with a 25-sample centered mean, then form the signal to project onto harmonic basis functions.

steps.title: Build the harmonic design
steps.text: Create cosine and sine columns at the requested period and its harmonics, and solve their coefficients by ordinary least squares.

steps.title: Add fitted basis terms
steps.text: The animation adds the already fitted weighted basis terms. This is an algebraic construction, not an optimization trajectory.

steps.title: Inspect the decomposition
steps.text: The trend, harmonic projection and remaining residual match the registered standalone operator.

parameters.name: trend_window
parameters.effect: Controls which structure remains after centered trend smoothing.

parameters.name: primary_period
parameters.effect: Sets the base harmonic period in sample units.

parameters.name: num_harmonics
parameters.effect: Adds paired cosine/sine columns. More terms increase representational capacity without guaranteeing better identification.

parameters.name: fit_scope
parameters.effect: The example uses the complete record. Prefix fitting estimates coefficients on the chosen prefix and evaluates the basis over the record.

cautions: The harmonic coefficients are fitted numerically, but this standalone operator has no trained neural backbone.
Changing the supplied period changes the basis. The algorithm does not establish that the period is physically correct.
The visual addition of basis terms is not the temporal sequence of a training algorithm.
Full-record smoothing and fitting require an appropriate information boundary before downstream forecasting.

references.title: Deng et al. (2024), Parsimony or Capability? Decomposition Delivers Both in Long-term Time Series Forecasting

trace_note: Intermediate arrays are computed with the implemented operator helpers. The final trend, season and residual are checked against public decompose(). The animation explains this standalone experimental block; its source architecture is cited for provenance.
input_note: Deterministic synthetic teaching signal; not a benchmark.

checks.validation_scope: One deterministic teaching input; no benchmark claim.
